title: kate-fileio: treat a Unicode line break as an ending
summary: to_wire_form writes the target ending for U+2028 and does not add a second ending. A trailing CR still counts. The test goes in the existing encode tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: encode.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Add is_unicode_break. The body is matches!(ch, '\u{000B}' | '\u{000C}' | '\u{0085}' | '\u{2028}' | '\u{2029}'). In to_wire_form, the newline arm becomes one condition: if scalars[i] == '\n' || is_unicode_break(scalars[i]). That arm still pushes opts.line_ending.as_str(). The ensure check becomes one if: if opts.ensure_trailing_newline && !s.is_empty() && !s.chars().next_back().is_some_and(|ch| ch == '\n' || ch == '\r' || is_unicode_break(ch)). Do not nest an if inside an if. Do not touch the CR LF pair skip, encode, write_bom, or encode_utf16_bytes. Update the comment on to_wire_form so a Unicode line break is an ending. You may update that comment. The existing test a_trailing_cr_counts_as_an_ending stays green. Do not rewrite its assertions. The test a_unicode_line_break_counts_as_an_ending uses to_wire_form with UTF-8, no BOM, Lf, and ensure true. The text a then U+2028 returns a then LF. The text a then U+2029 returns a then LF. The text a then LF stays a then LF. The text a then CR stays a then CR. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines. Run the full test module named in the commands, not only the new test.

regression_tests.name: encode::tests::a_unicode_line_break_counts_as_an_ending
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. a followed by U+2028 with ensure true becomes a, U+2028, and LF. After the change it is a and LF. A trailing CR still stays a CR.
